content.text: I’ll trace the invitation from the members settings page through creation, acceptance, and the system’s use of the new membership.

The acceptance path checks the stored token and invitation state, then creates membership before checking seats again. I also found a gap in the email flow: the service generates the raw token but doesn’t pass it to the mailer. I’ll distinguish the implemented behavior from the intended journey.

content.text:
The repository implements invitation creation and acceptance, but **the email-link handoff is incomplete**: the creation service generates a raw token, stores its hash, then discards the raw token without constructing or sending an acceptance URL. Here is the actual lifecycle, including that gap.

The members page starts in `src/app/(dashboard)/[orgSlug]/settings/members/page.tsx`, in its default `Page` function. It calls `loadTenantContext()` from `src/app/(dashboard)/[orgSlug]/_lib/tenant-context.ts`, which resolves the organization, obtains the signed-in user’s organization-scoped `Actor` through `getActor()`, asserts that the actor and organization agree, and evaluates feature flags. Actor resolution ultimately reads an active, non-archived membership. The page checks `can(actor, "member:read", …)` before displaying members, and `can(actor, "member:invite", …)` before displaying the invitation form. In `src/lib/permissions.ts`, `can()` delegates to `explain()`: cross-tenant access is rejected first, followed by the staff bypass and role matrix. Inviting requires at least `admin`.

The page also calls `listMembers()` and `billing-service.checkLimit(org.id, "seats")`. The resulting `LimitCheck` goes to `InviteMemberForm` in `src/components/domain/member/invite-member-form.tsx`. That component checks permission again, defaults the role to `member`, disables submission when seats are exhausted, and runs `inviteMemberSchema.safeParse()` in `handleSubmit()`. The schema in `src/schemas/member.ts` validates the organization ID, email, and role. `emailSchema` in `src/schemas/common.ts` validates an email of at most 254 characters and lowercases it; `invitableRoleSchema` in `src/schemas/role.ts` allows `admin`, `member`, or `viewer`, never `owner`.

Submission reaches `inviteMemberAction()` in `src/actions/members/invite-member.ts`. Its `withAction()` wrapper, defined in `src/actions/_lib/with-action.ts`, validates the payload again and resolves the actor from the supplied `orgId` through `requireActorFor()` in `src/lib/actor.ts`. This requires a valid session, a non-null active organization, an existing target organization, and active membership in it. The action handler then checks invitation permission, consumes one token from the organization’s `"member:invite"` rate-limit bucket, reads `getOrganizationSummary()`, and rejects if cached seat usage plus one exceeds `getPlanLimits(plan).seats`.

Next, `inviteMember()` in `src/server/services/invitation-service.ts` delegates to `inviteMembers()` with a one-item batch. That function checks organization scope and permission again, consumes rate-limit capacity again, requires the organization to exist, and checks seats using **active members plus pending invitations**, with `wouldExceedLimit()` from `src/config/plan-limits.ts`. Thus this page’s submission consumes the rate-limit bucket twice. Also, `countPendingInvitations()` currently counts every unaccepted, unrevoked invitation, including expired ones. There is no check here for an already-invited email or an email belonging to an existing member.

Only after those checks does `inviteMembers()` call `randomToken(32)` from `src/lib/hash.ts`. This creates 32 random bytes encoded as URL-safe base64. `hashToken()` produces its SHA-256 hexadecimal digest. `insertInvitation()` in `src/server/repositories/invitation-repository.ts` writes an `invitations` row containing a generated ID, organization ID, normalized email, granted role, inviter’s user ID, **token hash**, 14-day expiry, creation/update timestamps, and initially null `acceptedAt` and `revokedAt`. The table is defined in `src/server/db/schema/members.ts`, with a unique token-hash index. No membership row is created yet.

The service then emits `"member.invited"` with the organization, inviter, creation time, email, and role. `registerActivityListeners()` in `src/server/services/activity-service.ts` records the invitation in the activity log. The action invalidates the organization cache tag, and `withAction()` invalidates the `"members"` and `"invitations"` tags before returning an `ActionResult<Invitation>`.

**The raw token should travel in `/invite/<raw-token>`; the hash should remain in storage.** However, `toInvitation()` in `src/server/repositories/_mappers.ts` exposes `row.tokenHash` as the `Invitation.token` field defined in `src/types/member.ts`. That returned field is therefore a hash, not a usable acceptance credential: submitting it would hash it again. `InviteEmail()` in `src/emails/invite-email.tsx` can display a supplied `acceptUrl`, inviter, organization, role, and expiry, but the invitation service never invokes email rendering or sending and never supplies that URL. Even `sendEmail()` in `src/server/services/email-service.ts` only logs message metadata; it has no outbound mail transport.

If the colleague nevertheless receives a link containing the correct raw token, `/invite` is public in `src/proxy.ts`. The default `Page` in `src/app/(auth)/invite/[token]/page.tsx` first validates token syntax with `invitationTokenSchema` from `src/schemas/invitation.ts`: 32–128 characters, restricted to letters, digits, underscores, and hyphens. It does **not** look up the invitation or check expiry at this point. It resolves the session with `getSessionPrincipal()` from `src/lib/session.ts`; a signed-out visitor is redirected to login with `/invite/<token>` as the return destination.

A signed-in visitor sees `InviteAcceptForm` from `src/app/(auth)/invite/[token]/invite-accept-form.tsx`. Clicking “Accept invitation” sends the hidden token to `acceptInvitationAction()` in `src/actions/members/accept-invitation.ts`. That action validates the token again and requires a valid session, but does not require existing membership in the target workspace.

It calls `invitation-service.acceptInvitation(principal.userId, input)`, which hashes the submitted raw token and calls `findInvitationByTokenHash()`. This lookup is intentionally not scoped by a client-supplied organization: the matching stored invitation determines the organization and role. The service requires a matching row, then rejects revoked, already-accepted, or expired invitations, in that order. **It does not compare the signed-in user’s email with the invitation email or require email verification.** Possession of the token plus a valid session determines which user joins.

The service next calls `member-repository.findMember()`. If a non-archived membership already exists, it returns that row without marking the invitation accepted or emitting another join event. Otherwise, `insertMember()` creates an active `Member` with the stored organization, role, and inviter, the signed-in user ID, a join timestamp, null last-seen time, and creation/update timestamps. It then calls `markInvitationAccepted()` and emits `"member.joined"` with organization, accepting user as actor, occurrence time, membership ID, user ID, and role.

The rest of the system receives that event through listeners wired at startup by `src/instrumentation.ts` and `registerEventHandlers()` in `src/server/services/event-registry.ts`. `registerUsageListeners()` in `src/server/services/usage-service.ts` increments cached `seatsUsed`. The module-level `registerFanOut()` in `src/server/services/notification-service.ts` creates a `"member_joined"` notification for the organization owner through `notify()`, subject to recipient preferences and channel filtering. These subscribers run concurrently: `emit()` in `src/lib/event-bus.ts` awaits all of them settling and isolates their failures. There is currently no `"member.joined"` activity listener or automatic webhook listener, despite the event appearing in related type/schema vocabularies.

After creation and event delivery, `acceptInvitationAction()` calls `assertSeatAvailable()`. It resolves an actor from the new membership, reads the organization summary, and rejects if cached seats exceed the plan limit. **This check happens after the writes, with no transaction or rollback**, so an over-limit error can leave the membership created and invitation consumed.

On success, `InviteAcceptForm` routes to `/<orgSlug>` if the landing page received an `org` query parameter, otherwise `/orgs`. Acceptance does not change the session’s active organization. Subsequent workspace requests resolve the new membership through `session-service.resolveActorForOrg()`, obtain its stored role, and update `lastSeenAt`; permission checks now use that `Actor`. Organization listing through `organization-service.listOrganizationsForUser()` and `organization-repository.listOrgsForUser()` also discovers the workspace through the membership row.
